tables.caption: Key dates [ 39 ]
rows: Passage of the Early Parliamentary General Election Act 2019 through the House of Commons.
Passage of the Early Parliamentary General Election Act 2019 through the House of Lords.
Early Parliamentary General Election Act 2019 received royal assent and comes into force immediately. The Act set 12 December as the date for the next parliamentary general election.
Dissolution of parliament and official start of the campaign. Beginning of purdah. Royal Proclamation issued, summoning a new Parliament and setting the date for its first meeting.
Receipt of writ of election – legal documents declaring election issued.
Notices of election were given in constituencies.
Lists of candidates were published for each constituency.
Deadline to register for a postal vote at 5pm in Northern Ireland. [ 40 ]
Deadline to register for a postal vote at 5pm (Great Britain), [ 40 ] as well as registering to vote across the United Kingdom at 11:59pm. [ 40 ]
Deadline to register for a proxy vote at 5pm. Exemptions applied for emergencies.
Polling Day – polls opened at 7 am to 10 pm.
Results announced for all the 650 constituencies. End of purdah.

First meeting of the new Parliament of the United Kingdom, for the formal election of Speaker of the House of Commons and the swearing-in of members, ahead of the State Opening of Parliament 's first session. [ 41 ] [ 42 ] [ 43 ]
State Opening of Parliament and queen's speech.
